articles.title: How a cold pulse in the Northwest Atlantic reshaped East Coast fisheries
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Fishers in the Northeast began noticing an unusual shift in the summer of 2023. Some familiar catches, including shortfin and longfin squid, declined, while cold-water species such as mackerel bounced back from years of decline. A new study published in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans finds that a pulse of cold, fresh water brought unusually cold conditions to the region, disrupting fisheries from New England to the Mid-Atlantic.

articles.title: The bioeconomy is gaining ground worldwide, report shows
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Oil and natural gas still account for the vast majority of the world's energy and raw materials, with all the associated environmental and biodiversity consequences. The bioeconomy is an approach to overcoming this dependence: Instead of using fossil fuels, it uses renewable resources such as plants, microorganisms and organic waste. The goal is for economic growth to go hand in hand with protecting species, the climate and soils.

articles.title: Filling the gaps in global rainfall maps
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Global rainfall maps are built from observations collected by multiple satellites, but they have an important limitation. The satellites that provide these measurements cannot see the whole Earth at once. As a result, some regions of these maps can have no valid observations.

articles.title: Scientists finally uncover why statins can cause muscle pain
articles.summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising reason why statins, the widely prescribed cholesterol-lowering drugs that help prevent heart attacks and strokes, can sometimes cause muscle pain, weakness, and even severe muscle damage. Using advanced imaging technology, researchers discovered that statins can attach to a crucial protein in muscle cells and force open a channel that normally controls calcium flow. This causes calcium to leak continuously, potentially damaging muscle tissue.

articles.title: Hurricane warning maps are improving, but a dangerous problem remains

articles.title: Astronomers uncover new secrets of the Universe’s first five minutes
